subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the angle between the curves 2y² − 9x = 0 and 3x² + 4y = 0 in the fourth quadrant.

mark_split.label: Find the fourth-quadrant point of intersection

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), book p.219, chapter 10 APPLICATIONS OF DERIVATIVES, the TANGENTS AND NORMALS sub-section, Short Answer question 7(ii). recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say how many points the curves share, which one the question asks for and why, and what formula gives the angle.

steps.label: Find the fourth-quadrant point of intersection
steps.margin_note: Two marks. The elimination gives TWO common points, the origin and (2, −3). The question names the fourth quadrant, so the origin is set aside — it lies on the axes, in no quadrant.
lines: ⇒ y = 0  or  y³ = −27, that is y = −3
y = 0 gives x = 0, the origin, which lies on the axes and not in any quadrant.
y = −3 gives x = 2(9)/9 = 2, so the point is (2, −3), where x > 0 and y < 0.
∴ the fourth-quadrant point of intersection is P(2, −3).

recall.must_convey: That eliminating x gives y(y³ + 27) = 0, so y = 0 (the origin) or y = −3, and the fourth-quadrant point is (2, −3).

y to the fourth plus twenty seven y equals zero

the fourth quadrant point is two comma minus three

steps.why: The two curves meet at two points and the tangents at the origin are not the same pair as at (2, −3), so the answers differ. The question names the quadrant precisely because the point has to be chosen, and choosing it is where the marks are.
common_mistakes: Using the origin, which is a common point but lies in no quadrant.
Solving y³ = −27 as y = 3 and landing in the first quadrant.
Substituting y = −3 into 2y²/9 as −2, since y² is positive whatever the sign of y.
steps.memory_tip: Fourth quadrant means x positive and y negative — check the signs of the point against that before going on.

steps.label: Find both slopes there
steps.margin_note: Third mark. The first slope needs y and the second needs x, so both coordinates of P are used. Substitute only after differentiating.

differentiate the second curve to get minus three x by two

both slopes are negative at this point

steps.why: Each curve has its own tangent at the shared point, so two derivatives are needed. The first slope depends on y and the second on x, which is why the full coordinate pair from step 1 matters.
common_mistakes: Losing the minus sign when substituting y = −3 into 9/(4y).
steps.memory_tip: The curve with y² gives a slope in y; the curve with x² and a plain y gives a slope in x.

steps.label: Apply the angle formula
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Both slopes are negative, so their product is positive and the denominator 1 + m₁m₂ = 13/4. The 4s cancel and leave 9/13.
lines: If θ is the angle between the curves at P, then

recall.must_convey: That tanθ = |(m₁ − m₂)/(1 + m₁m₂)| = 9/13, so θ = Tan⁻¹(9/13).
accept: tan theta is mod of m one minus m two by one plus m one m two
minus three fourths plus three is nine by four

theta is about thirty four degrees forty two minutes

steps.why: The 4 in the numerator and the 4 in the denominator cancel, so the answer is a clean fraction. Keeping the working in quarters until the last line is what makes that cancelling visible.
common_mistakes: Taking the product of two negative slopes as negative.
Reporting the answer as Tan⁻¹(13/9) with the fraction inverted.
steps.memory_tip: Difference on top, one plus the product underneath, modulus around the whole fraction.

insider_note: The question names the FOURTH quadrant, so only the point with x > 0 and y < 0 is wanted — the other root is discarded. Find the intersection first, then the two slopes there.
